title: What is known about 1RB---_0LC0RB_1RA1LD_1LE1LF_1LB0LF_0RC0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0LC0RB_1RA1LD_1LE1LF_1LB0LF_0RC0LA.
intro: This six-state machine is a holdout of the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine moves numbers between binary counters, in nested loops that get deeper each epoch; it halts only if state A lands on a 1. No halt in the first 1011 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps of the run
claims.text: The shift rules the machine uses in its run (every sweep met when the symbolic simulator runs from many configurations of the run), each for every number of copies; for instance B erasing a run of 1s rightward.

claims.title: The transfer engine, every visit, every size
claims.text: An engine visit is A on the 0 of d in L' i e x i d R. The theorems prove the whole visit for every size: x = b becomes a, or x = a becomes b with a borrow over m digits a ending at a digit b, z (0000) or v (0100), which drops one step (b→a, z→b, v→z); and the right counter gets 1 with a carry over k ones (digits b/c), or across the separator S1 = e c g b e g, or across S1 and S2 = e c g c (12k+50 steps for x = b over k carries; 12j+12k+10m+240 for a borrow over m digits and a carry across S1). 12 theorems, 3 to 6 variables each.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 302 cells have been visited and 173 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct run of 10<sup>11</sup> steps without a halt.

claims.title: The same tapes as its twin
claims.text: At each of the 34 moments the head reaches a new cell in the first 1.5·10<sup>9</sup> steps, 1RB---_0LC0RB_1RA1LD_0RD1LE_1LF0LA_1LB0LE and 1RB---_0LC0RB_1RA1LD_1LE1LF_1LB0LF_0RC0LA have the same tape.

claims.title: The engine covers the whole transfer phase
claims.text: From step 9,410,541 to step 120,015,313 the head visits the engine (at cell −129) 1,023,987 times; all but 21 visits are instances of the theorems (the borrows that reach the left end read the blank cells as z digits). The 21 others are the overflows of the right counter.

claims.title: The right counter shrinks at each overflow
claims.text: The right counter has 19 digits (3 + 10 + 6, in three pieces). It first overflows at visit 499,692 (so it started at 24,596), and then after 2<sup>18</sup>, 2<sup>17</sup>, …, 16, 8, 8, 4, 2, 1 more visits: each overflow costs it a digit, and the phase ends at visit 1,023,987, when it has none left. The first overflow is the epoch at step 63,383,081.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.08). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.047).

claims.title: Transfers between counters, nested
claims.text: Read off the run: the engine moves 1 from a down-counting counter to an up-counting one at each visit; separators let carries through; each epoch adds a counter to the middle of the tape.

claims.title: The next epoch runs the same engine one level deeper
claims.text: In the reference machine, at step 3·108, the tape reads L1 i b e L2 i e i e x y d R (L1 13 digits, L2 6 digits): the two-digit counter x y counts down every visit, L2 every fourth, and the right counter, now with a one-digit piece in front (b/c e g …), counts up. Not yet proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts only if A reads a 1; the run is a growing nest of counter transfers whose epoch-to-epoch rule is not decoded.

claims.title: One visit function, shared by four machines
claims.text: A visit of E (the head at a cell in state E until it first steps left of it) on the mirrored tape (read right to left) uses only seven window rules in the run from blank tape, among them the doubler 1100 → 1100 with two visits passed on. The same seven rules come out for 1RB1RF_1RC0RF_0RD0LC_1LE1RA_1LC---_0LD0RE, 1RB1RF_1RC0RF_0RD0LC_1LE1RA_1LC---_1RB0RE and 1RB---_0LC0RB_1RA1LD_0RD1LE_1LF0LA_1LB0LE. No halt up to top visit 208 (tape 1,453,185 cells, visit counts up to 70,542 bits); the tape grows about 5% per top visit.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RF_1RC0RF_0RD0LC_1LE1RA_1LC---_0LD0RE up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine moves numbers from one binary counter into another, one unit per visit of its engine, in a nest of loops that gets one level deeper every epoch. It halts only if state A ever lands on a 1.

facts.text: No halt in a direct run.
By 7.3·10<sup>9</sup> steps, each one counter deeper.
The sweeps of the run, proved for every length.

sections.heading: A tape of words
html: Read the tape as words: a = 1000, b = 1100, c = 1110, d = 10, e = 110, f = 100, g = 11110, i = 11000. Every tape of the run is a sequence of them. The words a/b are binary digits 0/1 of counters that are counting down, b/c digits 0/1 of counters counting up, and e, g, i, d, f are separators.

sections.heading: Moving one number into another
html:
Most of the time the tape is L · i e x i d · R: a counter L (digits a/b, highest on the left, with x its lowest digit) and a counter R (digits b/c, lowest on the left). Every visit of the head to the engine takes 1 from L and adds 1 to R. Eight consecutive visits in the reference machine from step 9,937,953 (the right counter's first three digits):

stepL … xR (first digits)
9,937,953bbb bbbb
9,938,003bbb acbb
9,938,117bba bbcb
9,938,167bba accb
9,938,307bab bbbc
9,938,357bab acbc
9,938,471baa bbcc
9,938,521baa accc

(lean/Rules.lean, event_b: the visit with x = b and the lowest digit of R = b takes 50 steps and leaves x = a and that digit c.) The counter R is longer than it looks: after its first three digits come e c g b e g, ten more digits, e c g, seven more, and the carries cross the separators, so R is a 20-digit counter in three pieces. When R overflows, its carry reaches the right end of the tape; when L runs out, the borrow reaches the left end.

sections.heading: Epochs, each one level deeper
html:
The run goes in epochs. Each starts when the head reaches the right end with a burst of new cells (the tape grows by 45 to 61 cells at once); then come a visit to the left end, one more to the right end, one more to the left end, and a long quiet stretch:

epoch starts at steptape width

4,943,138183
66,904,148244
591,307,944297
2,120,776,816366

(reference machine; at 1011 steps the width is 516.) The time between epochs grows by factors of 98, 13.5, 8.8, 3.6, 3.5, and at the start of each epoch the middle of the tape holds one more counter than at the previous one: in the reference machine the words between the leading counter and the fixed tail bbbbbbbbbb e b i bbbbbbb ee ik are i, then ieai bbb eaibei, then ibebabaabieiebbibei bbbb eibei, then ibebbbbieibeibbeieieaieieabibei bbbb eibei, … with k = 5, 6, 7, … one more each epoch. The machine is running nested loops whose depth grows by one per epoch.

sections.heading: The transfer engine, for every size
html:
Each visit of the head to the engine i e x i d takes 1 from the left counter and adds 1 to the right one, and lean/Events.lean proves the whole visit, borrow and carry included, for every number of digits involved. The left counter has digits a = 0, b = 1 and two more, z = 0000 = 2 and v = 0100 = 3: a borrow turns the a's it passes into b's and lowers the first other digit by one step (b→a, z→b, v→z). The right counter is binary (b = 0, c = 1) in three pieces of 3, 10 and 6 digits, and its carries cross the separators e c g b e g and e c g c unchanged.

In this machine the transfer phase runs from step 9,410,541 to step 120,015,313: 1,023,987 visits, all but 21 of them instances of the twelve theorems. The 21 are the overflows of the right counter: the first at visit 499,692, then after 218, 217, …, 2, 1 more visits, because each overflow costs the counter one digit. When none is left, the next level starts: in the reference machine, at step 3·108, the engine reads L1 i b e L2 i e i e x y d, where a two-digit counter x y feeds L2, which in turn is fed by L1.

sections.heading: The halting transition
html: The machine halts only in state A reading a 1. A is entered from C0 (1RA, moving right) and from F1 (0LA, moving left). Every transition is used often (at least 2.6·107 times in 109 steps), so there is no rare moment to watch; halting needs an A step to land on a 1, which the word structure above never offers. Whether the nested loops can ever produce a word pattern that does is the open question.

sections.heading: What would settle it
html: Write the epoch as a recursive program on the list of counters: what each separator does when a carry or borrow reaches it, and what the head writes at the two ends. Then the epoch-to-epoch map is a formula, and the halting question is whether some counter can reach a value that puts A on a 1.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.08). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.047).
After 109 steps the tape spans 302 cells (264 left of the start, 32 right), with a density of 1s of 0.573.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RF_1RC0RF_0RD0LC_1LE1RA_1LC---_0LD0RE: rename A→E, B→C, C→D, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB---_0LC0RB_1RA1LD_0RD1LE_1LF0LA_1LB0LE: 8,947,615 configurations, the last at step 9,474,108 here and step 10,000,000 there

summary: Moves numbers between binary counters (digits 1000/1100 counting down, 1100/1110 counting up) one unit per engine visit, in nested loops one level deeper each epoch (family X, twin).
